newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf Air has no plans to change share structure.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Air has no plans to change share structure.

text.p: Debt-ridden Gulf Air has no plans to change the equity structure of the regional carrier owned equally by Qatar, Oman, Abu Dhabi and Bahrain, its chief said in remarks published on Sunday.

"There are no intentions to restructure the capital or the shareholders' equity which shall remain 25 percent for each of the four partners," Sheikh Ahmed bin Seif al-Nahayan told the London-based Arabic-language daily Asharq al-Awsat.
The shareholders, at the end of a meeting in Doha last week, brushed aside plans by Abu Dhabi to take over the company but asked partners to extend loans to ease a cash crunch.
It deferred plans to increase its capital by 100 million Bahraini dinars ($265 million) from 150 million dinars and left it up to each partner to decide on the size of the loan.
Abu Dhabi had offered to pump in fresh capital and loans to help the airline facing $2 billion in debt, in return for an increase in its shareholding, officials said.
But Qatar and Oman opposed the offer, fearing the move would allow Abu Dhabi to take control of the Manama-based carrier.
Sheikh Ahmed told the daily the company might make profits or break even in 1997 after it reduced staff, leased out some aircraft and closed uneconomic routes to boost efficiency.
"The company's monthly reports in the second half of 1996 clearly showed that," he said without giving figures.
